recognize_zh: 與左側淋巴球的核相比，大多數紅血球明顯偏小、中央淡染區擴大（hypochromia），並夾雜靶形細胞與少數細長細胞，符合小球性低色素紅血球（microcytosis）。
features: Red cells predominantly smaller than the nucleus of the lymphocyte (microcytosis)
Widened central pallor in many cells (hypochromia)
Scattered target cells and occasional elongated or teardrop poikilocytes
A lymphocyte and a monocyte provide size reference
Platelets are readily seen in the background
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a population of red cells that are mostly smaller than the nucleus of a lymphocyte, with increased central pallor. Mild to moderate poikilocytosis is present, including target cells and occasional elongated and teardrop forms. A lymphocyte and a monocyte are seen, and platelets are adequate to increased. Findings are consistent with microcytic, hypochromic red cells, as seen in iron deficiency or thalassemia; iron studies and hemoglobin analysis are needed to distinguish them.

ddx.vs: Iron deficiency favors pencil cells, marked anisocytosis and thrombocytosis with low ferritin, while morphology overlaps with thalassemia.
The presence of target cells raises thalassemia, which typically has a higher red cell count, lower RDW, basophilic stippling and abnormal HbA2 or globin gene testing.
Normocytic red cells approximate the diameter of a small lymphocyte nucleus with central pallor of about one-third, unlike the smaller hypochromic cells here.
